title: Westlake Robotics' WR1 Brain Has Two Humanoids Fold Trousers With Dexterous Hands
source_used: Pandaily (the pre-fetch returned 0 characters; the article body was read from the page's embedded data)
key_facts: Westlake Robotics, a Hangzhou company spun out of Westlake University, has released WR1, which it calls a general brain for humanoid robots.

In demonstration footage published on 9 Oct 2026, a humanoid running WR1 takes corn from a fridge, turns to an air fryer, tidies a basket and plush toys and straightens a quilt in the bedroom without stopping to reset between rooms.

WR1 combines a world model with a vision-language-action model to output one whole-body action sequence covering walking, torso posture and dexterous hand movement; a separate action expert called GAE keeps the robot balanced.
The company says most humanoids plan walking, posture and hand work separately and must stand still before using their hands.
In the main demo, a humanoid lifts trousers from a swaying rack and works with a second WR1 humanoid to pass, spread and fold them with dexterous hands.
Westlake Robotics calls this the first public demonstration of a humanoid fully folding clothing with dexterous hands; the claim has not been independently verified.
Earlier, WR1 folded clothes on a robotic-arm platform, reaching 36 seconds per item at its fastest according to the company.
Founded by Westlake professor Donglin Wang with co-founder Yue Zhang; it targets home service, manufacturing and specialized work.
